sections.title: Opening Narration
sections.instructions:
## Opening Narration
- Welcome everyone and thank them for joining
- Introduce yourself and the session topic
- Set time expectations for the session
- Acknowledge that this is designed for all experience levels
sections.transcript:
### Welcome

Hello everyone, and welcome. Really glad you are here today.

My name is [Trainer Name] and over the next [X] hours we are going to cover [Topic]. This session is designed for all levels - whether you have never touched this before or you are already using it and want to go deeper, there is something here for you.

sections.title: Module Outline
sections.instructions:

sections.title: Narration
sections.instructions:
## Narration
- Set up the conceptual foundation before demoing
- Explain why understanding the model makes the product easier to use
- Introduce two key ideas: [Concept A] and [Concept B]
sections.transcript:
### Setting the Stage

Before I show you the interface, I want to spend a few minutes on the underlying concepts. Trust me - once you understand how this works, everything you see in the demo will make immediate sense.

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.instructions:
## Concept Explanation
- Define [Concept A] and why it matters
- Explain the limitation of [Concept A] by itself
- Introduce [Concept B] as the mechanism that closes the gap
- Use a real-world analogy to make the model concrete
sections.transcript:
### What Is [Concept A]?

[Concept A] is the engine behind the product. Think of it as a very sophisticated pattern-matching system trained on a huge amount of [relevant data]. It learns to recognise and generate [output type] that sounds natural and accurate.

Here is the catch though: it was trained on data up to a certain point in time. Ask it something from last week and it simply does not know.

### Solving the Gap with [Concept B]

That is exactly what [Concept B] is for. Instead of relying solely on the trained model, [Concept B] lets the product fetch fresh information from [source] and incorporate it into the response in real time.

A good analogy: the trained model is like a very well-read expert. [Concept B] is like handing that expert today's newspaper just before they answer your question.

sections.title: Key Points
sections.instructions:
## Key Points
- [Concept A] = trained on historical data, strong at natural language
- [Concept B] = supplements the model with live or contextual data
- Together: accurate, up-to-date, context-aware responses

sections.title: Narration
sections.instructions:
## Narration
- Transition from concept to product
- Share URL/entry point
- Confirm sign-in requirement
sections.transcript:
### Into the Product

Alright, let's stop talking about it and actually go in. I am going to navigate to [URL] now - make a note of that, it is the most important thing to remember from today.

You will need to sign in with your [account type] account. If you are following along, do that now.

sections.title: Demo Steps
sections.instructions:
## Demo Steps
- Show the main interface and orient participants to key areas
- Open the [feature area] and explain each option
- Show the [setting] toggle and explain control behavior
- Run a sample interaction and unpack the output
sections.transcript:
### Orienting to the Interface

This is the main screen. Across the top you have [navigation area]. On the left is [panel]. The centre is where [main action] happens.

### Trying It Live

I am going to type [sample input] here and show you what comes back. Watch the [specific element] - that tells you [what it means].

*[Run the interaction]*

See that? The product returned [description of output]. Notice it also pulled in [additional context] - that is [Concept B] in action, exactly what we just talked about.

sections.title: License Comparison
sections.instructions:
## License Comparison
- Explain Tier 1 capabilities and boundaries
- Explain Tier 2 capabilities and additional data access
- Highlight specific capability unlocked in Tier 2
sections.transcript:
### Which Tier Do You Have?

Before you run off and try everything, let me be clear about what you have access to depending on your license.

**Tier 1 - included with [base product]:** You get [Feature set A]. The product can reach [public/web data source] to answer your questions. That is already very powerful.

**Tier 2 - the [add-on name]:** On top of that, you get [Feature set B], which means the product can now access [private/work data]. This also unlocks [specific capability].

If you are not sure which tier you have, [how to check]. The rest of today's demo works with Tier 1, so everyone can follow along.

sections.title: Narration
sections.instructions:
## Narration
- Transition to participant practice time
- Define the exercise goal
- Set collaboration mode (individual or pair)
- Ask participants to post outcomes in chat
sections.transcript:
### Your Turn

Alright, now it is your turn. I am going to give you about five minutes to try this yourself.

The goal is simple: [specific task description]. The steps are on the slide. When you have a result you are happy with, drop it in the **chat** - I want to see what everyone comes up with.

Work at your own pace. If you get stuck, Horan is watching the chat and will help you out.

sections.title: Narration
sections.instructions:
## Narration
- Open the floor for live questions
- Invite participants to unmute
- Keep chat open for additional questions
- Set a clear time boundary for the Q&A block
sections.transcript:
### Opening Q&A

Alright - that is the content for today. Well done everyone.

We have a few minutes now for live questions. If you have been holding something back, now is the time. Go ahead and **unmute** yourself and ask away. You can also keep posting in chat - Horan and I are both watching.

Who wants to go first?
